title: Weights of atoms in a finite probability law
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable, and let $s\subseteq\mathbb R$ be finite, with $X\in s$ almost everywhere. If $\lambda\ge0$ and $\mu(X=x)\ge\lambda$ for every $x\in s$, then the real atom weights sum to one, $\sum_{x\in s}\mu(X=x)=1$, and each satisfies $\mu(X=x)\ge\lambda$.
hypotheses_covered: $s$ is a finite subset of $\mathbb R$
replaced: Let $X$ be measurable on a probability space and supported almost surely on a finite set $s\subseteq\bbr$. If $\lambda\ge0$ and $\Pr[X=x]\ge\lambda$ for every $x\in s$, then the real atom weights $w_x=\Pr[X=x]$ satisfy $\sum_{x\in s}w_x=1$ and $w_x\ge\lambda$ for every $x\in s$.
